sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Matus, also written Matunus, was a British divinity. He was a bear deity who may have been a god or a goddess. Matus was honored at Risingham, just north of the great wall that the emperor Hadrian built. The wall guarded Britain from the aggressive tribes of the north. Matus may have been Pictish rather than Celtic.
objective: Document Matus, the bear deity honored at Risingham in Britain.
